solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go into school square — find something poisonous

indicators.note: the verb is placed into the school abbreviation, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt, a try
nine is the square of three

explanation.surface: A pupil is told to go into the school quad and track down something toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like a courtyard but is a number: nine, three squared.
explanation.definitionFit: Strychnine is a notorious plant-derived poison, an example of a deadly substance.

clue.text: Person that is dumped by Sally

indicators.note: the abbreviation is discarded from the longer word, leaving the remainder

parts.note: a sally is a sudden sortie by besieged troops
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone has been jilted by a woman named Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally reads as a girl's name but is a military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically a good sort is a decent individual, so the word can stand for a human being.

clue.text: Mineral in concrete covering over half of growing area

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, covering, the second

parts.note: concrete in the sense of actual, not abstract

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for a cultivated plot is used

parts.note: a garden is an area for growing plants

explanation.surface: A mineral is set in concrete laid over half of a vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Realgar is an orange-red arsenic sulphide ore, a mineral of the kind the clue names.

clue.text: This health professional may briefly suggest an Italian lake

definitions.text: This health professional may briefly suggest an Italian lake

parts.words: This health professional may briefly suggest an Italian lake
parts.note: shorten company to CO and doctor to MO and the two together spell Lake Como

explanation.walkthrough: Each word of the answer has a familiar two-letter short form, CO and MO, and those join to name Como, a lake in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic employed by a firm to look after its staff is a workplace health professional.

clue.text: Catmint eaten by one pet apparently

indicators.note: the letters are swallowed up inside the following words of the clue

explanation.surface: A household pet seems to have eaten some catmint.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepeta is the botanical genus name for catnip and its relatives, the plants cats love.

clue.text: Dancer terribly skinny I judge should be tucking in

indicators.note: the judge's letter is tucked into the middle of the rearranged letters
terribly suggests the letters are badly mangled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A very thin speaker thinks a judge should eat more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' shuffles the letters of SKINNY and I, and 'tucking in' puts J among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaslav Nijinsky was the celebrated Russian ballet star of the Ballets Russes.

clue.text: Nick heading off for island

indicators.note: the first letter, the word's head, is removed

parts.note: to nick is to steal, to pinch

explanation.surface: A cut or notch is removed, leaving a place surrounded by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick here is the British slang verb for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island, found in many place names.

clue.text: Excellent bishop, this person's a name for revolutionising country

indicators.note: turning round the whole string, so it is read from the end backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the setter speaking of themself: I'm, this person is

explanation.surface: A fine bishop announces he has a name for a nation in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of A1 is taken as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a nation in south-west Africa, so it fits as an example of a state.

clue.text: Spooner's name for pet rabbit, similar creatures being wild animals

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: bunny is the pet word for a rabbit
hares are close relatives of rabbits

explanation.surface: Spooner coins a name for his pet rabbit and its relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BUNNY HARES gives something said like 'hunny bares'.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey bears is a popular name for kinkajous or sun bears, untamed mammals.

clue.text: Notice graduate in work following right plan

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay comes after, following, the letter for right
the notice and the graduate go in the word for work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
an ad, advert, is a notice
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone spots a graduate at work following the correct scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A road map figuratively means a strategy or set-out course of action.

clue.text: Mary runs, coming in sixth out of twelve — one to swear?

indicators.note: the shuffled name comes inside the month abbreviation

parts.note: June is the sixth of the twelve months, abbreviated JUN

indicators.note: the name runs, its letters flowing into a new order

explanation.surface: Mary runs a race and finishes sixth of twelve, enough to make anyone curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one to swear?' suggests cursing, but the oath here is the juror's oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A juror takes an oath before trial, so this member of a jury is one who swears.

clue.text: Turning violently on traitors, men protest

indicators.note: the letters are turned about wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: Men object as they savagely round on a group of traitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstration is a forceful objection or complaint, a noun meaning an act of protest.

clue.text: Many a gunboat may be deployed to protect a harbour

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround and shield the extra letter
the letters are deployed, put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Gunboats are sent out to guard a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Guantanamo Bay is a large sheltered inlet in Cuba, a natural anchorage for ships.

clue.text: Working at basic lab giving fresh opportunity for university don?

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Lab work gives an academic a new chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Academics are granted periods of paid leave for study or travel, a break from teaching.

clue.text: Cockney gets duck, Poplar's no. 2 being caught in gully

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the name

parts.note: a Cockney would say Harry as 'Arry, dropping the H

indicators.note: the second letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: An East Ender in Poplar is caught in a ravine with a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop their H, so Harry becomes 'Arry; Poplar is an East London district. A duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: An arroyo is a steep-sided dry stream bed, a ravine in the American South-West.

clue.text: Panic about potassium in cosmetic treatment

indicators.note: the word for panic goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: a scare is a moment of panic
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: Someone panics over potassium in a beauty product.
explanation.definitionFit: Care of the complexion with creams and lotions is a beauty regime for the face.

clue.text: Good girl protected by fellow explorer

indicators.note: the inner letters are sheltered inside the word for fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nice girl is looked after by a male explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan led the first expedition to sail round the world, a famous navigator.

clue.text: Presentation rude, not one to entertain old women

indicators.note: the remaining letters host, entertain, the new ones inside
the Roman numeral for one is dropped

parts.note: rude in the sense of brutish, bestial

explanation.surface: A crude show, with nobody on hand to host the old ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' drops the I from BESTIAL to leave BESTAL, and 'to entertain' puts OW inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestowal is the formal giving of a gift or honour, a conferring of something.

clue.text: Something bony presents problem when eating bird

indicators.note: the word for problem swallows, eats, the bird

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Something with lots of small bones causes trouble when you eat a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the flat bone in the centre of the chest, a part of the skeleton.

clue.text: State of senselessness in places after retreat by soldiers

indicators.note: the soldiers stand by, next to, the turned word
the word moves back, read from its last letter

parts.note: to put is to place, so places is puts
OR, Other Ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A daze sets in at various places after soldiers pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state in which a person is barely conscious.

clue.text: Signal before appearance of wise man

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A sign heralds the arrival of a wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foreshadow or portend, giving warning of something to come.

clue.text: Highest point of a river leading to exclamation of surprise

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
gee is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: The summit of a river's course produces a cry of amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Apogee is the furthest point of an orbit from Earth, figuratively a peak or climax.

clue.text: New teacher to help rival educational establishment?

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newly arrived teacher helps out at a competing school.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford and Cambridge people traditionally refer to the rival university by this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an Oxbridge idiom for the competing university, a jocular nickname.

clue.text: Brutal person won't want son round

indicators.note: the letter is not wanted, so it is removed

parts.note: a beast is a brutal person

explanation.surface: A cruel man has no use for his son hanging around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a link to the son, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's beat is the regular route patrolled, a circuit or route walked.

clue.text: Essential Conservative charm lacking heart?

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to charm is to enthral

explanation.surface: A Tory may be charming but heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something central is core or key, of chief importance to the whole.

clue.text: Dire expression when first hint of fear is expressed?

definitions.text: Dire expression when first hint of fear is expressed?

parts.note: dire means grim

indicators.note: expressed in its sense of squeezed out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a face is a facial expression, as in pulling a face

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a dreadful face the moment a flicker of fright sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed' means squeezed out: the F is pressed out of FACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial look, the kind of pained look fear produces.

clue.text: Weak material

definitions.meaning: ... meaning feeble or unconvincing, as a ... excuse
a fabric woven with metallic threads, glittery cloth for evening wear

explanation.definitionFit: Lame is feeble, as in a poor excuse; lamé is a glittering fabric with metal threads.

clue.text: Captivity of any number in underground activity

indicators.note: the number letter goes in the word for burial

parts.note: interment, burial, puts things underground
N stands for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Any number of people are imprisoned in an underground operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Internment is confinement of people, especially without trial, so it means imprisonment.
